questions.q: Why did the Congress party dominate Indian politics in the years after Independence?
answer: In the first three general elections after Independence, the Indian National Congress won overwhelming majorities, creating an era of one-party dominance. Several factors explain this.

answer.text: The Congress had led the national movement for independence and enjoyed enormous prestige and goodwill among the people. Its leaders were seen as the heirs of that struggle, which gave it a natural advantage at the polls.

The Congress was a broad, umbrella party that brought together people of different religions, castes, classes, languages and ideologies. By accommodating diverse interests and factions within itself, it absorbed much of the potential opposition and appealed to almost every section of society.
The opposition parties were small and divided, while the Congress had a strong, nationwide organisation reaching down to the villages.

answer: Importantly, this dominance was won through free and fair democratic elections, not by suppressing rivals.
